title: Wayve end-to-end driving
summary: A driving stack learned from data rather than written as explicit rules.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Wayve trains neural networks to map sensor input directly to driving behaviour, arguing that this generalises better than hand-coded perception and planning pipelines. It raised US$1.05bn in 2024 and licenses its software to automakers instead of operating fleets. Validation is the hard part: an end-to-end system is harder to inspect when something goes wrong.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Pilot
Estimated window 2024–2030
Confidence label Researching
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

End-to-end driving shifts cost from engineering to data and validation; the safety case becomes the product.

What Would Change The View

  • OEM production contracts.
  • Regulatory acceptance of learned systems.
  • Edge-case performance in new cities.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
